narration.say: The safety net spread the crash.
Microsoft just explained how Outlook went down worldwide.
A hidden bug froze servers that got too busy.
When one froze, its traffic shifted to the others.
The neighbors overloaded, froze, and passed it on.
In two hours, over 80 percent of North American servers froze.
Then traffic spilled into every other region.
Rerouting needs spare room, so Microsoft plans walled-off server pools.
Follow Media Diet for the physics behind the headlines.

shots.beat: first frame / hook: a perspective row of paper gateway servers freezing one after another through a glowing red rerouting net; "THE SAFETY NET / SPREAD THE CRASH."
superhook: a generic paper laptop stuck on "Can't connect" while queued mail piles up; "≈ 24 hours of disruption" + report date chip
the bug: one server in cutaway; requests queue at a one-at-a-time lock (turnstile) that jams under load; the server frosts over
rerouting: ten servers fed by one mail stream; one freezes and its traffic shifts to the rest (same traffic ÷ fewer servers)
cascade: the neighbours cross the limit line one by one and freeze, passing their load on (illustrative numbers)
North America: stylised paper world map, server sites going dark outward from US East until over 80% are unresponsive
worldwide: traffic arcs spill from North America to every other region and their sites go dark
payoff 1: with spare servers the same failure is absorbed (gauges stay under the limit)
payoff 2: paper walls rise between pools; a failure stays inside one pool (Microsoft's planned fix)
CTA: Media Diet sign flips up
